newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta investment scheme reports profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Malta investment scheme reports profit growth.

text.p: Santumas Shareholdings Ltd, a collective investment scheme, made an operating profit of 34,722 Maltese pounds ($92,000) in the six months to October 31, 1996, directors said in an interim report.
There were no strictly comparable figures for the six months to October 1995.
The company made a profit of 61,999 pounds for the 12 months to April 30, 1996, and said it expected profits for the year to April 1997 to exceed 100,000 pounds.
The scheme is licensed by the Malta Financial Services Centre.

"The markets were going very much with us. During the period from May 1 to October 31 the FTSE share index went up by 3.38 percent, the Malta index rose 10.9 percent and sterling was up 5.98 percent against the Maltese lira.
"Overall, by way of appreciation, profits and dividends, our portfolio made 47,651 pounds or 11.49 percent," the report said.
Net earnings per share for the six months were 3.26 cents against 3.52 cents for the whole of the previous year.
Santumas Shareholdings was set up in 1963 and has a portfolio of shares primarily on the London stock market and holdings in various Maltese listed and unlisted companies.
